items.claim: The letter disclosure puts this poem's pe-before-ayin swap after Lam.2.18-Lam.2.19 when the swapped pair stands behind the span at Lam.2.16-Lam.2.17, and the addressee options held open include one the pointed bytes exclude, on a span that quotes no Hebrew at all.
items.evidence: Acrostic: the letters named for the span are right - the verse-initial consonant is tsade at Lam.2.18 and qof at Lam.2.19 - but the swapped pair sits at the 16th and 17th letters, pe at Lam.2.16 and ayin at Lam.2.17, one and two verses BEHIND the onset, so placing the swap later in this poem is byte-false; the positions of tsade and qof are indeed untouched by it. Addressee: the third option offered, the speaker's own heart, is excluded at the bytes - Lam.2.18 opens with לִבָּ֖ם (oshb:Lam.2.18, byte tier, "their heart"), a masculine noun with a 3mp suffix standing as subject of a 3ms perfect, while the commands that carry the stretch - הוֹרִ֨ידִי (oshb:Lam.2.18, byte tier, "let down") at Lam.2.18 and the four imperatives of Lam.2.19 - are 2fs throughout, which that noun cannot govern; the two feminine candidates inside חוֹמַ֣ת בַּת צִ֠יּוֹן (oshb:Lam.2.18, byte tier, "wall of the daughter of Zion") are correctly left open, and the bytes do not separate them. Engagement: no Hebrew is quoted anywhere in the grounds, and the vocative the reading rests on is a feature of the rendering - the construct chain carries no vocative particle, so the only byte evidence for direct address is the 2fs morphology just named. Both sides of the front seam: 2fs address to the city is already running before the seam (צָרָֽיִךְ (oshb:Lam.2.17, byte tier, "your adversaries")) and continues through the span, an undisclosed straddling device; what is new at Lam.2.18 is the imperative mood, not the addressee, so the seam holds on a narrower ground than the one stated. Checked and correct: SAMEKH at Lam.2.17, Lam.2.18 and Lam.2.19 (single-witness, tier-3 weak), the one paseq segment at Lam.2.19 cited as a bare count, and the K/Q note at Lam.2.19 disclosed; the rendering quoted for that verse does however sit on the qere word, so calling the variant unengaged understates it.

items.claim: Two recurrence claims that carry the close are asserted with no ref, tier or digit, while the single digit given is attached to a form standing once book-wide that is nonetheless labelled a refrain, and the mark layer is routed into the substrate-signal keys.
items.evidence: Refrain label: בְּי֥וֹם אַף יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier, "in the day of the anger of Yahweh") collates at byte tier and its digit is right - the phrase stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse) - but a form attested once cannot function as a refrain, and this stretch both names it one at the poem close and carries a refrain key for it. Wrath recurrence: the claim that the close returns to the wrath of the poem's own alef line carries no ref, no tier and no digit; at the bytes the alef line reads בְּאַפּ֤וֹ (oshb:Lam.2.1, byte tier, "in his anger"), a suffixed form, and Lam.2.21 carries a second-person suffixed form, so the close and the alef line share no attested spelling: the bare token stands in 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, Lam.2.3 and Lam.2.22, finals-normalized), while the consonantal string stands in 11 verses (sweep: 11 verses, finals-normalized), a homograph-laden review list that takes in the word for ashes at Lam.3.16 and the nostrils sense at Lam.4.20 and is therefore no count of the anger sense at all; the claim is defensible at root level and is asserted at no level. Petition recurrence: the assertion that the opening petition repeats an earlier one is likewise unanchored, although the byte evidence is exact and available - רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.2.20, byte tier, "see, Yahweh, and look") stands verbatim in 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, Lam.1.11 and Lam.2.20, finals-normalized skeleton tier), which is the strongest single ground for this onset and is the one omitted. Signal keys: a PE-mark key sits among the substrate signals, which puts the single-witness mark layer inside the signal taxonomy; the mark facts themselves are right (PE at Lam.2.22, SAMEKH at Lam.2.19-Lam.2.21) and their prose disclosure is complete. Voice: the 1cs speaker and 2ms addressee are byte-visible (עוֹלַ֣לְתָּ (oshb:Lam.2.20, byte tier, "you have done"), טִפַּ֥חְתִּי (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier, "I have cared for")), but nothing in the morphology separates the city's voice from the narrator's, whose own 1cs already stands in this poem (עֵינַי֙ (oshb:Lam.2.11, byte tier, "my eyes"), with 1cs verbs addressing the city at Lam.2.13); a high confidence on a unit type defined by that identification is not carried by the bytes. Letters resh, shin and tav and their order are correct, and the seam itself is sound - Lam.2.19 is 2fs imperative address and Lam.2.20 turns to 1cs speech with 2ms address - though the command to pour out the heart before the Lord and the prayer that follows it bind across that seam undisclosed.

items.claim: Every ground offered stands at or before the onset: the close at Lam.3.9 into Lam.3.10 carries no evidence and no disclosure although the same third-person affliction chain and the same 1cs-suffixed noun straddle it, and the letter-order note is attached to letters the order does not touch.
items.evidence: Close seam: the cited grounds are the onset in both witnesses and the poem end behind it; nothing is offered at the close. At the bytes the cut falls inside a continuous chain - Lam.3.2 through Lam.3.16 runs one pattern of third-person divine agency with 1cs object suffixes and no addressee anywhere, the 1cs statement at Lam.3.14 standing inside it - and דְּרָכַי֙ (oshb:Lam.3.9, byte tier, "my ways") stands on both sides of the cut, at Lam.3.9 and Lam.3.11 (that token stands in 3 verses book-wide, sweep: 3 verses, Lam.1.4, Lam.3.9, Lam.3.11, finals-normalized token tier, of which Lam.1.4 is the construct plural of another phrase; inside this poem only the two verses flanking this seam). Weighing both sides: the gimel triplet does close an enclosure image (גָּדַ֤ר (oshb:Lam.3.9, byte tier, "he walled up") opens Lam.3.7 and Lam.3.9 alike, sweep: 2 verses, finals-normalized token tier) and the triplet boundary is respected, so the cut is permissible - but a byte-true device straddling a unit's own seam argues continuity until it is disclosed, and it is not. Letter order: the pe-before-ayin note is attached to the alef, bet and gimel triplets, where the order fact is inoperative - the swapped pair in this poem is the 16th and 17th letter set, at Lam.3.46-Lam.3.48 and Lam.3.49-Lam.3.51, far outside the span. Disclosure scope: the paseq and mark sentence reaches past this span to characterise what other stretches of the poem disclose, which is not a property of this unit. Checked and correct: the onset splice at byte tier; the three triplets and their letters; the absence of any paseq segment in this poem; and the mark set - this poem carries a mark only on each triplet's closing verse (22 marked verses of 66), so Lam.3.3, Lam.3.6 and Lam.3.9 is the complete in-span set, with the PE at Lam.2.22 behind the onset. A high confidence with no close-seam evidence is not calibrated.

items.claim: The span is warranted by an unbroken voice across Lam.3.10-Lam.3.18, but Lam.3.17 carries a form that is 2ms or 3fs at the bytes and is read as direct address to the deity by the translation, an ambiguity the grounds neither disclose nor resolve.
items.evidence: Voice: Lam.3.17 opens וַתִּזְנַ֧ח (oshb:Lam.3.17, byte tier), a form identical for 2ms and 3fs, with נַפְשִׁ֖י (oshb:Lam.3.17, byte tier, "my soul") available as its feminine subject, so the pointed bytes admit both a direct address to the deity and a statement about the speaker's own soul. The translation cited elsewhere in this stretch takes the first: “You have removed my soul far away from peace.” (web:Lam.3.17). This is the only verse in Lam.3.10-Lam.3.18 where any second person arises - everything around it is 3ms with 1cs object suffixes, or 1cs speech at Lam.3.14, Lam.3.17b and Lam.3.18 - so a same-voice warrant that never weighs it is incomplete, and the choice bears directly on where this stretch begins. Extent: the byte-tier splice at Lam.3.18 covers two words while the rendering paired with it covers the whole quoted clause, including the words for perished strength; splice extent and gloss extent are not matched. A whole-book superlative for that line is carried with no digit and nothing byte-checkable behind it. Checked and correct: the splice collates at byte tier; the dalet, he and vav triplets and their letters; the K/Q note at Lam.3.10 disclosed by count with no slice taken there; and the marks at Lam.3.12, Lam.3.15 and Lam.3.18 with the preceding triplet's mark at Lam.3.9, which is the complete set for this poem's triplet-closing mark layer.

items.claim: The chapter-wide singularity claimed for the turn at Lam.3.21 is contested by the bytes, since the identical three-token turn stands again at Lam.3.24 inside the same span and is left undisclosed.
items.evidence: עַל כֵּ֥ן אוֹחִֽיל (oshb:Lam.3.21, byte tier, "therefore I will hope") recurs at Lam.3.24, where the same three tokens are followed by a prepositional phrase: the string stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, Lam.3.21 and Lam.3.24, finals-normalized skeleton tier). Naming Lam.3.21 the pivot line of the whole chapter is an exclusivity claim over a 66-verse poem carried with no sweep beside it, and the one byte fact bearing on it points the other way. The omission also costs this stretch its best internal evidence: the twice-stated turn binds the zayin and het triplets to one another, which is precisely the question held open here. Weighing both sides of the front seam: Lam.3.18 closes on a declared end of expectation while Lam.3.21 and Lam.3.24 state a hope twice, so the repetition supports the choice actually made and is left unused. Checked and correct: the splices at Lam.3.19, Lam.3.21 and Lam.3.22 all collate at byte tier; the tet triplet does open all three of its verses on the same word (sweep: 3 verses, Lam.3.25-Lam.3.27); the letters and their triplets; the K/Q note at Lam.3.20 disclosed by count with no slice taken there; the marks at Lam.3.21, Lam.3.24 and Lam.3.27 with Lam.3.18 behind the onset; and the disputed extent of the hope turn is disclosed honestly at a low-confidence setting with a frontier flag rather than decided.

items.claim: The close is warranted by a shift into third-person argument, but both sides of Lam.3.33 into Lam.3.34 are third person at the bytes, and at the onset the antecedent of the three subjectless verbs is left on the far side of the seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: Person: no 1cs and no 2ms form stands anywhere in Lam.3.28-Lam.3.39. Lam.3.28-Lam.3.30 are 3ms with 3ms suffixes (יֵשֵׁ֤ב (oshb:Lam.3.28, byte tier, "let him sit") and two further 3ms verbs); Lam.3.31-Lam.3.33 are three clauses of the same conjunction about the Lord; Lam.3.34-Lam.3.36 are three lamed-infinitives governed by אֲדֹנָ֖י לֹ֥א רָאָֽה (oshb:Lam.3.36, byte tier, "the Lord has not seen"). So no person, number, speaker or addressee changes across the stated seam and the ground as written is not carried. What does change is clause type, and that change is produced by the acrostic letter itself (the kaf triplet forces the conjunction openers, the lamed triplet the infinitives), so it is not an independent signal. Both sides: the bytes argue continuity rather than a break - the two triplets are negated predications about one subject, the divine title standing at Lam.3.31 and again at Lam.3.36, each with the negative (the adjacent pair of title and negative stands in 3 verses book-wide, sweep: 3 verses, Lam.2.2, Lam.3.36, Lam.3.37, finals-normalized). A triplet-boundary cut here remains permissible; it needs a ground the bytes carry. Onset: the three verbs of Lam.3.28-Lam.3.30 have no expressed subject anywhere in the span, and their nearest antecedent is לַגֶּ֔בֶר (oshb:Lam.3.27, byte tier, "for the man"), one verse beyond the onset (that token stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide, sweep: 1 verse, finals-normalized token tier; its consonantal string in 5, sweep: 5 verses, Lam.1.16, Lam.3.1, Lam.3.27, Lam.3.35, Lam.3.39, finals-normalized); the onset ref names that verse and states no ground for it. Checked and correct: the splice at Lam.3.31 collates at byte tier; the yod and kaf triplets and their letters; the K/Q note at Lam.3.32 disclosed by count with no slice taken there; and the marks at Lam.3.30 and Lam.3.33 with Lam.3.27 behind the onset. A high confidence with one seam unwarranted and the other mis-stated is not calibrated.

items.claim: The headline device, a pair of rhetorical questions in succession at the close, is not what the bytes carry: the two interrogative-marked lines are separated by a verse whose question status exists only in the translation.
items.evidence: The mem triplet's interrogatives are the opening words of Lam.3.37 and Lam.3.39; between them stands מִפִּ֤י עֶלְיוֹן֙ לֹ֣א תֵצֵ֔א (oshb:Lam.3.38, byte tier, "from the mouth of the Most High does not come"), which carries no interrogative particle at all. The two are therefore not in succession, and on the translation's reading of Lam.3.38 as a question the count is three rather than two; either way the stated pair is wrong, and a question count that depends on the rendering cannot corroborate a close. The pairing is carried into the substrate-signal keys as well. K/Q: the note at Lam.3.39 is disclosed and the Hebrew splice does stop short of the variant word, as stated, but the rendering quoted for that verse does render the qere, so the stated scope is narrower than the quoting actually done. An original-language ref is listed at Lam.3.39 with no Hebrew engagement at that verse. The onset repeats a contrast the bytes do not carry: Lam.3.28-Lam.3.33 is third person throughout, so a turn into third-person argument at Lam.3.34 is not a person change. Checked and correct: the splice at Lam.3.37 collates at byte tier; the lamed and mem triplets and their letters; the marks at Lam.3.36 and Lam.3.39 with Lam.3.33 behind the onset; the cohortative reading of the following triplet is byte-true (נַחְפְּשָׂ֤ה (oshb:Lam.3.40, byte tier, "let us search"), with two further 1cp cohortatives in that verse); no first-person form stands anywhere in the six verses; and the category deviation is disclosed in one sentence as required.
